name: CR-Int-15-partialfrac-2.c
questiontext: By expressing the integrand as the sum of its partial fractions, find the following definite integral: \[ \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}}. \] [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback: In order to calculate this integral we need to express \[{{CT:2}}\] as the sum of its partial fractions. Omitting details we have \[{{CT:2}} = {{CT:4}},\] hence, \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \int {{CT:4}} d{{CT:3}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:5}} \int {{CT:6}} d{{CT:3}} + {{CT:7}} \int {{CT:8}} d{{CT:3}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:9}} + {{CT:10}} +c \end{array}\] Recall that if \[\int f(x) dx = F(x)\] then \[\int^a_b f(x) dx = F(a) - F(b).\] Then, \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle F({{CT:0}}) - F({{CT:1}}) \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:11}} - [{{CT:12}}] \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:13}} \end{array}\]
